title: Watch: how an agent chooses its next step
points: An agent uses tool results to choose what to do next.
For our operator: study request → solver → result checks → human review.
caption: Official Google Cloud Tech concept video. The grid mapping is an original teaching analogy.
note: Play 0:43 to 3:28, a two-minute-forty-five-second excerpt. The publisher’s chapters cover the meaning of agentic behavior and workflow examples. Explain the distinction: a fixed workflow follows routes set in code; a model-based agent chooses some next steps using the information returned so far. Connect this to our grid example: an operator states a study goal, the agent calls a numerical solver, reads the result and either requests another allowed step or reports back. The solver performs the engineering calculation. The operator keeps the operating decision. These grid roles are our teaching analogy, rather than a claim that the video demonstrates grid control.
